1. The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
in Crime No.155/2021 of Bagepalli Police Station, Chickballapura District, registered for the offences punishable under Section 376 of IPC and Section 4, 6 and 17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Chandana.

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Nagendra B., learned Counsel for the petitioner and Sri Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials placed on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1.
She is innocent and has not committed any offence as alleged.
She has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
She was apprehended on 14.06.2021, since then she is in judicial custody.

4. It is alleged that accused No.4 has committed the penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl,
repeatedly.
The petitioner is the mother of victim girl.
No such allegations are made against the petitioner.
Accused No.3 and 4 are in judicial custody.
The victim is examined as P.W.1.
She has not alleged anything against the petitioner.
The other witnesses are only the mahazar and official witnesses.
Petitioner is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the petition.
She is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, prays for allowing the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
Victim is hardly aged 13 years.
She is the daughter of the present petitioner.

Petitioner had availed loan of Rs.10,000/-
from accused No.4 and therefore, the petitioner permitted accused No.4 to commit the offence.
It is a heinous crime which is alleged against the petitioner being the mother of victim.
The medical and FSL report support the contention of the prosecution.
P.W.1 has categorically stated that the petitioner was permitting accused No.4 in her house.

Without the help of the petitioner, the crime Smt Prabavathi vs State Of Karnataka on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187340786/
2 could not have been occurred.

sentences.text: Looking to the nature and seriousness of the offence and since other witnesses are yet to be examined, petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 7.
Petitioner is the mother of unfortunate victim aged 13 years.
It is the contention of the prosecution that the petitioner had availed loan of Rs.10,000/- from accused No.4 and he used to visit her house everyday.
Under such circumstances, he used to commit penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl very oftenly.
This allegation is supported by the evidence of the victim who is examined as P.W.1.
When the incident had occurred in the house of the petitioner, she cannot disown her responsibility.
Committing of such offence repeatedly by accused No.4 could not have been possible, unless the petitioner extends her helping hand.
Therefore, I am not ready to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner.
8. C.W.2 is the sister of the victim girl.
She is yet to be examined before the Trial Court.
The medical report discloses that hymen was not intact.
Under such circumstances, the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that there is nothing on record against the petitioner, cannot be accepted.
The petitioner being the mother had not protected her own child from sexual assault, which is more serious than committing the offence.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for bail as the same would adversely effect the evidence that is to be led by the prosecution.
Moreover, release of the petitioner on bail may not be in the best interest of the victim girl.

Hence, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
